hypothesis: W-R22's perfect mask-aware classification might rely on exact (0,0,0,0) missing-row encoding. Test fixed learned model across alternate erasure sentinels. Explicit multi-sentinel row recognition may generalize, but the original zero-only feature should not be assumed to.
science: Same fully observed four-channel input and positive/negative paired temporal task, no new semantic or sensor information.
freeze: Freeze three erasure values, two missing-tick counts, three source generators, two unseen swap types, feature arms, fresh heldout seeds, and all success criteria before original scientific execution.
dev: Train original W-R22 development model on original affine seeds240..255, 1728 examples, fixed original zero-erasure augmentation, 16 weights+bias, 32 epochs, LR 0.1. No heldout updates and no W-R22 heldout reuse.
arms: naive_augmented: frozen W-R22 trained naive model and existing naive top-two feature
maskaware_zero_only: frozen W-R22 trained mask-aware model, zero-only feature

maskaware_declared_sentinel_vocabulary: same frozen maskaware_zero_only weights but skip transition edges incident to rows equal any of three preregistered full-row missing values; no retraining and no per-example oracle missing-mask input
success: SENTINEL_VOCABULARY_TRANSFER if declared-vocabulary arm accuracy >=0.85 in ALL six nonzero-sentinel generator×erasure-value pooled conditions AND exceeds zero-only accuracy by at least 0.10 aggregate on nonzero sentinels. PARTIAL if declared vocabulary > zero-only by 0.05 but fails strong threshold. NEGATIVE otherwise.
controls: All positive and negative pairs share candidate first row and multiset
Swap occurs only at unmasked rows 11/12 or 13/14
Do not treat legitimate observed all-four-channel sentinel-equivalent rows as oracle-marked; document potential aliasing
No extra learned weights, train examples, epochs or model calls
No first-use retry or reuse of exposed heldout cohorts, exact SHA freeze, one full repo regression
claim_limit: Finite synthetic observation-missingness encoding; not a general perceptual or cognitive system.
